brief.data: Cruise RV Halcyon Point HP27-03, 10 days (Mar 8–17, 2027), 18 science berths. prompt:
I need the front end for Cruiseplan Commons. A shared planning document service that a university marine field station uses so several labs can jointly write the cruise plan for each research vessel expedition before it goes to the ship operator.

Who's using it: Dr. Kenji Moriyama, a second-year postdoc in a biological oceanography lab. His PI, the cruise's chief scientist, has handed him day-to-day coordination of the cruise plan. He knows the science and the vessel well but is new to refereeing between four labs' competing demands.

What they're doing right now: The plan is due to the vessel operator Friday. Overnight, a physical oceanography student and a sediment coring PI both edited the station schedule for Days 4–5 and claimed the same 14 hours of wire time at stations 18–22. Kenji needs to see exactly what each person changed and when, check who is working in the document right now (the coring PI is in it from a conference in Lisbon), and settle the overlap in comments. He then has to lock the station schedule section so only the chief scientist can change it. Meanwhile two undergraduates still need comment-only access to the berthing section.

What's in the system at this point: Cruise RV Halcyon Point HP27-03, 10 days (Mar 8–17, 2027), 18 science berths. Four participating labs (Moriyama/Arce bio-oce, Lindqvist physical, Duarte sediments, Benavides chemistry) have 22 named participants with roles: chief scientist, lab PI (editor of own sections), coordinator, student (comment only). The document has 9 sections: objectives, personnel and berths, station schedule, equipment and deck layout requests, hazardous materials, sample storage, data management, safety, and contingency days. The schedule has 31 stations with coordinates, planned arrival times, operations (CTD, multicore, net tow, mooring recovery) and wire-time estimates. 63 comments, 11 unresolved. Version history has 214 edits from the past 3 weeks, 9 of them since midnight. Currently present: Kenji, Dr. Duarte, and one student viewing.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
